blocks.name: Integrating Other Functions (Trig, ln & e etc)

blocks.text: Is integration the reverse of differentiation?

blocks.md:
- Yes, but remember “+c”, the constant of integration …

  - … unless finding a definite integral
- Recognising common results helps to make integration easier (See Differentiating Other Functions)
- You are given all the standard integrals in the formula booklet

blocks.alt: Notes diff_results, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.text: How do I integrate e<sup>x</sup> and e<sup>kx</sup>?

blocks.alt: Notes ex, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.md:
- The gradient of **e**<sup>**kx**</sup> is **ke**<sup>**kx**</sup>

  - ie **y = e**<sup>**kx**</sup>, **dy/dx = ke**<sup>**kx**</sup>
- The reverse applies when integrating
- This is an example of **reverse chain rule**

blocks.alt: Notes ekx, AS & A Level Maths revision notes
Notes ln, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.md:
- Remember **1/x = x**<sup>**-1**</sup>

  - The method for integrating powers does **not** apply if the power is -1

blocks.text: How do I integrating sin x and cos x?

blocks.alt: Notes sin_cos, AS & A Level Maths revision notes

blocks.md: - Note the minus in the integral of **sin x**

blocks.text: How do I integrate tan x?

blocks.md: - The integral of **tan x** is **ln|sec x| + c**

- Recall that $\frac{d}{dx}(\mathrm{tan}^{-1}x)=\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}$
- Then $\int \frac{1}{1 + x^{2}} \mathrm{d} x = \tan ^{- 1} x + c$ and $\int \frac{1}{a^{2} + x^{2}} \mathrm{d} x = \frac{1}{a} \tan ^{- 1} ( \frac{x}{a} ) + c$

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Make sure you have a copy of the formula booklet during revision but don't try to remember everything in the formula booklet.
- However, do be familiar with the **layout** of the formula booklet – you’ll be able to locate quickly whatever you are after, and you do not want to be searching every line of every page!
- For formulae you think you have remembered, use the booklet to double-check.
